mechanism: FOMC decisions are pre-positioned: rate-path expectations are already priced in over the days before the statement (a documented pre-FOMC drift), so the announcement itself carries little genuinely new information for a market that has been running up into it on 'cut/hold priced in' positioning. Once the statement lands with no incremental dovish surprise, there is no confirming catalyst to hold the pre-meeting long positioning together, and the unwind is not a one-bar reaction — it plays out over the following days as leveraged longs built during the run-up get stopped out, funding stays positive against them, and momentum/CTA-style flow extends the move. This is a calendar-anchored, multi-day 'sell the news' drift, not a same-bar volatility spike.
counterparty: Leveraged perp longs (and 'FOMC pivot' options buyers) who added risk into the meeting expecting a dovish confirmation or rate-cut catalyst. When the statement gives them no incremental win, they are stuck holding pre-priced-in longs with no new buyer behind them; over the following days they are forced out by stop-losses, margin calls, and the funding/carry cost of holding a long that stopped working, and that forced de-risking is the flow a resting short captures across the week after the meeting.
prediction: On the long_1h train era, shorting the universe at the next open after the closed 1h bar covering each FOMC statement release (see signal_py FOMC_EVENTS, all within 2025-06-27..2026-04-24), TP 200 / SL 200 bps, max hold 168 bars (7 days), yields net_bps_mean > 0 with bootstrap CI95 (bootstrap_ci.mean_ci) excluding 0, and observed WR >= fee_math.p_star(200) = 0.52875, with n >= 30 pooled across the 19-symbol universe. Falsified if CI95 includes 0, if WR < p*, or if n < 30 given only 6 calendar events in the train window.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 7 killed day-of-week / weekend / CME-gap / Saturday-alt calendar effects as mostly null after FDR and stale. This thesis is not a weekday or weekend seasonal regularity; it fires on 6 specific pre-scheduled FOMC statement timestamps in a 10-month window and holds a full week, a completely different calendar object (a discrete monetary-policy event, not a recurring weekday/session pattern).

Row 84 killed FOMC/CPI momentum because it needed 1-minute precision to trade the announcement-bar reaction itself. This thesis deliberately does NOT trade the announcement bar or its immediate volatility spike; it enters at the next 1h open after the statement and holds for 7 days, targeting the multi-day post-announcement drift, which is computable on the bot's slower cadence and does not need minute-level timing.

Row 76 was multi-day MEAN REVERSION, dead post-2022. This is a multi-day MOMENTUM/continuation short conditioned on a specific macro calendar event, not a reversion-to-mean bet, and has no reversion premise.

evidence: Stocktwits, 'Bitcoin Price Fed FOMC Meeting History...' (opened): crypto chartist Ardi is quoted reporting that in the week following 8 of the last 9 FOMC meetings, Bitcoin dropped an average of 11% over the following 7 days ('an average drop of 11% in the 7 days post-FOMC'); the single exception (May 2025) followed a meeting where BTC had already fallen ~24% from its all-time high beforehand, i.e. the pre-meeting positioning was already washed out. Phemex, 'BTC Dropped After 8 of 9 FOMC Meetings' (opened, independent write-up of the same practitioner pattern): documents the same 8-of-9 count within a 48-hour post-announcement window across the 9 meetings from May 2025 through April 2026, average decline ~5.6% across the eight negative instances (range 1.6%-8.6%), with concrete examples (Oct 2025 ~$126,000 -> $118,700, -5.8%; Jan 2026 ~$90,400 -> $83,383, -7.8%), and attributes it to a 'sell the news' dynamic since rate expectations are priced in ahead of the meeting. ScienceDirect, Corbet et al.-type 'Do FOMC and macroeconomic announcements affect Bitcoin prices?' (abstract page opened): establishes the academic baseline that FOMC announcements are a priced macro-event for Bitcoin, supporting that the mechanism (pre-positioning around a scheduled monetary event) is real and not solely a practitioner narrative, though neither of the two practitioner sources gives a formal bootstrap CI and both describe the same 2025-2026 sample window, so this prediction must be confirmed independently on long_1h train data via research.swarm.lib before any verdict. Funding caveat (not separately quantified here, per fee_math not covering it): a 7-day hold crosses ~21 funding settlements; net-bps math at grading time must add realized funding drag on top of fee_math.C_BPS, which this thesis's p_star check does not yet include.

import pandas as pd

# FOMC decision-day (second day of the 2-day meeting) closed 1h bar covering the
# ~2pm ET statement release, used as the short-entry trigger. Times are hardcoded
# public Fed calendar dates converted to UTC (EDT=UTC-4, EST=UTC-5); this is
# calendar metadata, not derived from price, so it carries no lookahead risk and
# is identical whether or not future bars are present (causality-safe).
FOMC_EVENTS = [
    "2025-07-30 18:00",
    "2025-09-17 18:00",
    "2025-10-29 18:00",
    "2025-12-10 19:00",
    "2026-01-28 19:00",
    "2026-03-18 18:00",
]

_EVENT_SET = {pd.Timestamp(ts, tz="UTC") for ts in FOMC_EVENTS}


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    out = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    fire = df.index.isin(_EVENT_SET)
    out[fire] = -1
    return out
